classification.difficultyReason: Construct radii to the intersections, recognise equilateral triangles to derive the sector angles, and express the lens as two sectors minus triangles.

content.prompt: Consider two circles of radius 1, each of which passes through the centre of the other circle. Find the area of the region that is common to both circles.

spec.description: Two equal circles with horizontal centre separation equal to their radius. Only the common lens is shaded.
spec.mathematics: Both radii are 1; centre separation is 1; intersection points are (1/2, ±sqrt(3)/2).
spec.answerVisibility: No centres, construction lines, angles or answer values are shown.

answer.short:
$\dfrac{2\pi}{3}-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$ square units.

Subtract the two triangles from the two $120^\circ$ sectors.
answer.worked:
Join the centres to either intersection point. Each resulting triangle is equilateral, so the common chord subtends $120^\circ$ at each centre. Its distance from either centre is $\tfrac12$, and its length is $\sqrt3$.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{sector}}&=\frac{120}{360}\pi(1)^2\\A_{\text{sector}}&=\frac{\pi}{3}\\A_{\text{triangle}}&=\frac12\times\sqrt3\times\frac12\\A_{\text{triangle}}&=\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\\A_{\text{common}}&=2\left(\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\right)\\A_{\text{common}}&=\frac{2\pi}{3}-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.\end{align*}$$
